transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-22 16:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom (rec)
Attendees: Sophie Clarke (Redwood AE), Mateo Ruiz (Redwood SE), Anika Bose (Redwood SE), Jenna Park (Cedar Head of Platform), Malik Hassan (Cedar Infosec), Priya Nair (Cedar DPO), Tom Liao (Cedar ML)

Summary (auto): kickoff to scope POC focused on prompt-level data sanitization, logging/redaction, and perf/latency benchmarks. Primary success criteria: remove PII from stored prompts, p95 latency below 220ms for standard convo workload, throughput to support 400 reqs/min peak, cost target < $X per 1M tokens.

Topics: success criteria, workload sizing, redaction approaches, retention windows, benchmark plan, timeline

[00:00] Sophie: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I see most folks are here — hi Jenna, Malik, Priya, Tom, and from our side Mateo and Anika. we want to run through goals for the pilot, sizing, and the data handling constraints.
[00:22] Jenna: yeah this is an important one for us. we need to prove we can use Redwood without shipping PII out to the hosted logs, and also meet our latency SLA for the customer chat flows.
[00:35] Malik: just to be clear, our compliance bar is SOC 2 plus internal policy that raw prompts with PII cannot be retained more than 7 days unless redacted. we may be okay with 30 days for anonymized telemetry.
[00:50] Mateo: perfect, thanks. quick note: Redwood supports both prompt redaction on ingestion and a no-persist mode for prompt storage. redaction can be rule based and ML based; we typically combine regex for deterministic items and NER for things like names and free-form addresses.
[01:10] Priya: do you have examples of your redaction accuracy? like false negatives — names slipping through?
[01:18] Anika: we have an eval set we've run internally; numbers vary by entity type. for phone numbers and ssn patterns regex is near perfect; names are trickier but combined NER+heuristic boosts recall to ~95% on our test corpora — but we should validate on your data.
[01:38] Tom: is the NER stage run in your hosted control plane or in the private VPC option? we have concerns about sending raw prompts to any central plane.
[01:47] Sophie: good Q. two options: 1) hosted POC where prompt redaction happens in-region and we mark the prompt as redacted before any long-term storage, or 2) private POC (VPC deployment) where the preprocessing/redaction runs inside your network — in that case nothing leaves your VPC except aggregated metrics.
[02:05] Jenna: that private path is the preferred target long term. but for POC we can evaluate both to compare performance and operational overhead.
[02:15] Malik: what about crypto? KMS integrations? audit logs?
[02:20] Mateo: we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM via API). encryption at rest is default, and audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. audit logs include token-level cost and request traces but we can configure redaction on those logs too.
[02:40] Priya: retention — we want minimal retention on prompts. for POC can we set retention to 0 days for raw prompts and 30 days for anonymized telemetry?
[02:48] Sophie: yes, policy is configurable per-project. for POC we can set prompt retention to 0 (no persisting raw prompt) and keep aggregated telemetry for 30 days. note: some debugging requires short-term ephemeral storage — we can enable ephemeral traces with strict access and auto-delete.
[03:05] Jenna: ok let's talk success criteria. from our side: 1) zero PII in persisted prompts across a 2-week data sample, 2) p95 latency < 220ms for the 2k token upper bound in our chat flows, 3) throughput sustaining 400 requests/min with <=5% error, 4) cost estimate for 1M tokens < internal threshold.
[03:30] Mateo: we'll run a benchmark harness to simulate the exact traffic — we ask you to provide representative prompt distributions, average token counts, and peak concurrency windows. we usually target p95 and p99. for the POC we'll aim for p95 < 200ms on dedicated small cluster and measure hosted as baseline.
[03:50] Tom: our typical prompt length is 60-120 tokens, but with full conversation history bursts hit 1800 tokens. do you have guidance for handling long context?
[04:02] Anika: yes, KV cache and selective context trimming are things we use. note the runtime chooses kernels based on sequence distribution; long sequences are more expensive and will affect throughput. for the benchmarks we'll produce a sequence mix config.
[04:20] Malik: messy transcription note: somebody said KV cache but the transcript writes "kay vee cache" earlier, lol.
[04:28] (laughter)
[04:30] Sophie: for redaction approaches we propose three phases during the POC: 1) deterministic filtering (regex) applied at ingestion, 2) ML NER pass for fuzzy entities, 3) post-response scrub to remove any generated PII leakage — and we'll log hits as redaction events.
[04:52] Priya: about post-response scrub — can that be applied before any logs or traces are stored? we need that guarantee.
[04:58] Mateo: yes, the post-response scrub is synchronous before any persistence. if the scrub fails or uncertain we can route that request to an isolated flow that does not persist the prompt and flags for manual review.
[05:12] Jenna: what about false positives — redacting too aggressively and harming model performance? we can't break intent.
[05:18] Anika: we include a "redaction confidence" score and a policy to only remove low-confidence tokens or to replace with placeholders. part of the POC is building a small eval set where we measure utility drop after redaction; success criteria should include a delta threshold (e.g., <5% change in top-1 accuracy on our eval prompts).
[05:42] Tom: benchmarks — what metrics will Redwood run vs what we should run?
[05:46] Mateo: Redwood will run latency distributions (p50/p95/p99), tokens/sec, concurrency, error rates, and cost per 1M tokens. we ask you to run functional correctness checks, and we'll collaborate on a shared spreadsheet so each run includes the same seed prompts. I'll upload the harness to the shared folder.
[06:06] Sophie: link refs: Mateo will add bench harness ("cedar-bench-v1") and redaction evaluation template to the shared drive — we'll put link in follow-up.
[06:14] Malik: timeline?
[06:16] Sophie: proposed: week 1 (2026-03-23 to 03-29): onboarding and data exchange, configure redaction rules; week 2 (03-30 to 04-05): run initial hosted benchmarks + redaction eval; week 3 (04-06 to 04-12): private/VPC perf run if agreed; week 4 (04-13 to 04-19): consolidation, report, and exec review.
[06:36] Priya: that timeline is tight but doable if we provide sample data quickly.
[06:40] Jenna: what does success look like to close to dedicated contract? is there a specific throughput threshold?
[06:45] Sophie: for Dedicated we usually commit to predictable throughput; for your use case we expect Dedicated to meet the 400 reqs/min target with margin. the pilot helps set the committed capacity. post-POC success would be a contract for Dedicated with 99.9% uptime and SLA latency guarantees.
[07:02] Tom: security reviews — can you send the full list of compliance docs now? we have a security evaluation checklist and procurement timeline.
[07:09] Sophie: yes I'll attach SOC2, network diagrams for private control plane, KMS integration guide, and our data flow diagrams.
[07:16] Malik: for procurement we also need a redaction test report showing sample prompt vs redacted result.
[07:22] Mateo: we'll generate one during the initial eval.
[07:25] (slight cross talk)
[07:28] Priya: a note on legal: we want contractual language about not storing PII and indemnities for leakage. legal will engage if the POC looks good.
[07:35] Sophie: understood. we'll surface our standard privacy addendum and we can negotiate retention clauses for the pilot.
[07:40] Jenna: OK quick recap?
[07:43] Sophie: recap — deliverables and owners: Sophie share docs and pricing; Mateo upload benchmark harness; customer to provide sample prompts and PII patterns; run hosted bench week 2 and private bench week 3; success criteria: zero persisted PII, p95 < 220ms, throughput >= 400 reqs/min with <5% error, tolerance for model utility loss <5% after redaction.
[08:10] Malik: sounds good.
[08:12] Tom: one more Q — if redaction misses something and we detect it post-facto, what's the incident process?
[08:18] Mateo: standard incident flow: immediate revoke of retention, manual purge, root cause analysis, and incident report. for the POC we can add an automated purge playbook to the runbook.
[08:30] Priya: we'll want to see that playbook.
[08:33] Sophie: we'll include it in the follow-up packet.
[08:36] (wrap up)
[08:38] Sophie: thanks everyone. we'll send the follow-up with links and schedule the benchmark kick off.
[08:42] Jenna: thanks all.

End of transcript.

Shared artifacts mentioned: cedar-bench-v1 harness (to be uploaded), SOC2.pdf (attached in follow-up), KMS-integration-guide.md, redaction-eval-template.csv, procurement-checklist.xls
